_comment: All web UI help text lives here. Keys are referenced by data-help="key" in index.html / app.js. Keep each to 1-2 short sentences.
nav.labs: Browse the lab catalog, build a lab in CML and check your solution.
nav.builder: Create or edit your own labs with a form or raw YAML.
nav.settings: CML connection, console access for live checks, lab options and the optional AI generator.
nav.more: Less common tools: AI lab generation, the AI prompt and the lab JSON Schema.
more.ai: Generate a lab with an OpenAI-compatible API configured in Settings. Optional.
more.copyPrompt: Copies a complete prompt for any AI chatbot. Import the YAML file it returns.
more.schema: Opens the JSON Schema that lab files follow (useful for editors and AI tools).
theme: Switch between light and dark mode.
import.button: Import a .encorlab lab pack, a .encorcourse course or a lab .yaml file. It is validated right away and appears in the list.
import.drop: Drop one or more lab or course files anywhere on this page to import them. Invalid files show what to fix.
filter.search: Filter labs by title, summary, id or blueprint item (e.g. 3.2.b).
filter.domain: Show only labs from one ENCOR exam domain.
filter.diff: Show only labs with this difficulty (1 = easy, 5 = hard).
filter.source: Built-in labs ship with the app; imported labs are your own or shared packs.
lab.item: Open this lab to see the task and build or check it.
lab.build: Imports the lab into CML as ENCOR-<lab>, starts it and waits until every node has booted.
lab.check: Grades your work on the running lab. Read-only: only show and ping commands are used.
lab.mode: Auto tries the live console and falls back to config. Live = device state over SSH; Config = running config via the CML API.
lab.reset: Wipes all devices back to the starting configs and restarts the lab. Your changes are lost and revealed hints are hidden again.
lab.destroy: Stops and deletes this lab from CML. Your history in this app is kept.
lab.edit: Open this lab in the Lab builder. Built-in labs open as a copy.
lab.export: Download this lab as a .encorlab pack you can share or import elsewhere.
lab.delete: Remove this imported lab from the app. It does not touch CML.
lab.status: Lab state in CML and how many nodes have finished booting. Updates while a job runs.
lab.timer: Starts automatically on Build and pauses when you solve the lab. Stored in this browser only.
lab.timerReset: Set the timer back to zero.
lab.task: What to configure. Interface names match the device image chosen in Settings.
lab.objectives: The checks the grader runs. Open only if you want spoilers.
lab.hint: Reveal a hint for this check.
lab.results: Pass/fail per check with what was found or missing. Expand output to see the raw device output.
lab.output: Raw output the check looked at.
lab.activity: Progress log of the current or last Build, Check, Reset or Destroy.
lab.history: Your previous check scores for this lab (last 50): hints used and whether it was a normal attempt, fault practice or an exam.
lab.historyClear: Delete the score history of this lab.
b.new: Start a blank two-router draft. The current draft is discarded.
b.load: Open an existing lab in the builder. Built-in labs open as a copy you can save.
b.cml: Start a draft from a lab already in your CML (IOL or IOSv nodes, ports 0-3).
b.validate: Strict offline test: applies the solution and requires 100% with it and 0% on the starting config.
b.replace: Allow saving over an imported lab with the same id.
b.save: Validate and save the lab to your labs folder. It shows up on the Labs page.
b.testlive: Builds a temporary ENCOR-TEST copy in CML with the solution applied, grades it, then deletes it. Save first.
b.tabForm: Edit the lab with form fields.
b.tabYaml: Edit the same lab as YAML. Changes are validated as you type.
b.yaml: The lab file. Use %if0%..%if3% (long) and %if0s%..%if3s% (short) instead of interface names.
b.validation: Validation result for the current draft: errors to fix, and offline scores per image and mode.
f.id: Unique lowercase id with dashes, e.g. ospf-stub-area. Also the folder name.
f.title: Title shown in the catalog.
f.domain: ENCOR exam domain, used for filtering.
f.blueprint: ENCOR 350-401 blueprint items, comma separated, e.g. 3.2.b.
f.platforms: Device images this lab supports. Use both unless a feature needs one.
f.author: Optional author name.
f.summary: One line shown under the title in the catalog.
f.task: Markdown instructions for the student. Write %if0% etc. for interfaces.
f.preview: Preview the task as students see it, with real interface names for the chosen image.
node.name: Hostname/label, e.g. R1. Renaming updates links, checks and the solution.
node.kind: router = IOL / IOSv; switch = IOL-L2 / IOSvL2.
node.x: Horizontal position on the CML canvas.
node.y: Vertical position on the CML canvas.
node.config: Starting config the student gets (addressing, no shutdown). Never the answer.
node.solution: Reference solution: config lines added on top of the starting config. Used by Test lab.
link.node: Node at this end of the link.
link.port: Data port 0-3; port N is %ifN% (Ethernet0/N on IOL, GigabitEthernet0/N on IOSv).
check.add: Add a check. Templates are pre-tested against real IOS output; custom checks use your own regex.
check.id: Short unique id for this check, e.g. r1-nbr-r2.
check.command: Read-only command to run (must start with show or ping).
check.match: Regexes (one per line) that must all be found. Multiline: ^ and $ match per line.
check.absent: Regexes (one per line) that must NOT appear in the output.
check.minSuccess: For ping checks: minimum success rate in percent.
check.description: What the check verifies, shown in results. Templates fill this in if empty.
check.hint: Shown to the student when the check fails or they click Show hint.
cml.use: Create a builder draft from this CML lab. Add checks and a solution before saving.
ai.desc: Describe the lab: topic, number of routers, difficulty, blueprint items.
ai.go: Ask the configured AI provider. The result is validated (up to 2 automatic retries) and opens in the builder.
ai.copy: Copy the prompt with your description filled in, for use in any AI chat.
ai.log: Progress of the AI generation, including validation errors sent back for fixing.
s.cml_url: Address of your CML server, e.g. https://cml.example.ts.net.
s.username: Your CML login (same as the CML web UI).
s.password: CML password, kept in memory only unless you tick Remember. Leave blank to keep the saved one.
s.remember_password: Store the password in Windows Credential Manager / Linux Secret Service so you don't retype it.
s.verify_tls: Keep On for a valid certificate (e.g. Let's Encrypt). Off only for self-signed test servers.
s.console_host: Host name where CML's console SSH server (port 22) is reachable. Blank = same host as the CML URL.
s.console_port: SSH port of the console server, or of your TCP passthrough proxy in front of it. Default 22.
s.grading_mode: Default for Check. Auto uses the live console if reachable, otherwise the running config via HTTPS.
s.platform: Image used for new builds. IOL is lighter and boots faster; IOSv is the classic image.
s.node_limit: Refuse to start a lab if running nodes would exceed this (your CML license limit).
s.show_help: Show the small help icons next to labels. Button tooltips stay available either way.
s.aiSection: Optional: let the app generate labs through an OpenAI-compatible API. Copy prompt for any AI works without it.
s.ai_preset: Fill in base URL and model for a known provider. You can still edit them.
s.ai_base_url: OpenAI-compatible API base URL ending in /v1.
s.ai_model: Model name as the provider expects it.
s.ai_api_key: API key for the provider. Kept in memory unless you tick Remember; never written to settings.json.
s.remember_ai_key: Store the AI API key in the OS keyring.
s.save: Save settings. Non-secret values go to settings.json; secrets only to memory or keyring.
lab.hintNext: Reveals the next hint, vaguest first. Hints you have opened stay visible for this lab until you click Reset.
lab.hintsBox: Hints you have revealed so far. The number of hints used is saved with each Check in History.
lab.revealSolution: Shows the root cause, the exact fix per device and the solution config. You will be asked to confirm first.
lab.solutionPanel: What the reference solution changes and why it works. Shown automatically when you score 100%.
f.solutionSummary: Markdown shown after a 100% score or on Reveal solution: the root cause, the exact fix commands per device, and why it works.
f.hints: Progressive hints, one per line and vaguest first, for the Hint button. If left empty, the check hints are used in order.
lab.break: Rebuilds the lab with a working config plus one random predefined fault, for unlimited troubleshooting practice.
lab.faultBox: The symptom you have to troubleshoot. The cause stays hidden until you fix it or reveal the answer.
lab.faultReveal: Give up and show the cause and the fix of the current fault. This is recorded as revealed.
lab.faultEnd: Stop fault practice. The devices keep their configs; click Reset afterwards to go back to the starting configs.
lab.faultPanel: What was broken and the exact fix. Shown when Check passes during fault practice, or after Reveal.
lab.faultConfig: The IOS lines that were applied on top of the working config to create the fault.
nav.progress: Your progress: mastery per ENCOR exam domain and topic, streak, time spent and weakest topics.
p.refresh: Reload the dashboard from your results history.
p.mastery: Weighted by the exam domain weights. Hints and revealed answers lower the score that counts.
p.solved: Labs you have scored 100% on at least once, out of all labs in your catalog.
p.streak: Days in a row with at least one Check, ending today or yesterday.
p.time: Estimated from the lab timer value sent with each Check.
p.faults: Break my lab faults you fixed (Check passed during fault practice).
p.domains: Mastery per exam domain from the 350-401 ENCOR v1.2 topics, with the official exam weight.
p.weakest: Topics with the lowest mastery. Open one of the labs listed to practise them.
p.items: Every blueprint item your labs cover, with mastery and the labs that train it.
p.activity: Number of checks per day over the last 30 days. Hover a bar for the date.
p.failed: The checks you have failed most often across all your attempts.
p.recent: Your last checks. Counted is the score after the hint penalty, or the exam result.
p.openLab: Open this lab on the Labs page.
filter.course: Show only the labs of one installed course, in the course's study order.
lib.open: Open the lab library: your courses with progress, plus labs and courses published online that you can install with one click.
lib.courses: Courses you installed: an ordered set of labs with your progress through it.
lib.course: A course bundles labs in a study order. Solved means the lab scored 100% at least once.
lib.continue: Open the first lab of this course that you have not solved yet.
lib.filter: Filter the lab list to this course, in course order.
lib.removeCourse: Remove this course and optionally the labs it imported (built-in labs and your history are kept).
lib.online: Lab packs and courses published in the project's GitHub repository (labs/ folder); loading it is the only time the app contacts GitHub.
lib.url: Address of a library index.json (https only). The default is the official library in the project repository.
lib.load: Download the library index and show what you can install.
lib.default: Go back to the official library address.
lib.install: Download this item, check its sha256 and size against the index, then validate and install it (courses include their bundled labs).
lib.integrity: Integrity check: a download whose sha256 or size differs from the index is rejected and nothing is installed.
lib.fromUrl: Install a .encorlab or .encorcourse file shared by someone else, straight from an https link.
lib.fileUrl: https link to a .encorlab, .encorcourse or lab .yaml file (max 20 MB).
lib.sha: Optional but recommended: the sha256 the author published. If it does not match, nothing is installed.
lib.installUrl: Download, verify and install the file from the link.
lab.consoles: Open device consoles: a link to this lab in the CML web UI and a ready-to-paste console server command per node (shown once the lab exists in CML).
lab.openCml: Open this lab in the CML Workbench in a new browser tab (log in to CML if asked). Right-click a node there, then Console.
lab.copyConsole: Copy the SSH command for this node's console. Paste it in a terminal and log in with your CML username and password.
lab.copyAllConsoles: Copy the console commands of all nodes at once, one per line.
more.updates: Ask GitHub whether a newer ENCOR Lab Builder release exists. Nothing is downloaded or installed.
s.check_updates: Off by default. When on, the app asks GitHub Releases at most once a day for a newer version (nothing is installed).
s.updateNow: Check GitHub Releases for a newer version right now (one anonymous request to api.github.com).
s.releaseLink: Open the release page on GitHub to read the changes and download the new version.
lab.exam: Exam mode: a timed, one-shot attempt with the solution withheld and hints disabled or costing points. You get a score report at the end.
lab.examMinutes: Time limit in minutes (5-240). The default depends on the lab's difficulty and size.
lab.examHints: Allow hints at a cost (each hint subtracts points from the final score) or disable them completely.
lab.examPenalty: Points subtracted from the exam score for each hint you use (0-50).
lab.examStart: Start the countdown now. Build the lab first if it is not running yet.
lab.examCancel: Close this panel without starting an exam.
lab.examBox: The exam countdown. When it reaches zero your lab is submitted automatically.
lab.examAbort: Abandon the exam. Nothing is recorded, and hints and the solution become available again.
lab.examSubmit: Grade the lab once and end the exam. The score report shows the raw score, hint penalty, time used and pass/fail.
lab.examReport: Exam score report: final score (raw score minus hint penalty, 0% if late) against the 80% practice target.
lab.snapshots: Save the devices' running configs and restore them later, e.g. before trying something risky. Read over the CML API; nodes must be BOOTED.
lab.snapName: Optional name made of letters, digits, dot, underscore or dash. Blank uses the date and time.
lab.snapNote: Optional note to remember what this snapshot contains.
lab.snapSave: Read the running config of every device in this lab and save it as a snapshot.
lab.snapRestore: Stop, wipe and reboot the lab with this snapshot's configs. Unsaved changes on the devices are lost.
lab.snapView: Show the saved configs of each device.
lab.snapDownload: Download the snapshot as a text file with one '! device NAME' section per device.
lab.snapDelete: Delete this snapshot (the lab is not changed).
lab.snapDevice: Saved running config of this device.
lab.report: Open a printable report of this lab in a new tab: latest check per objective, exam result, attempt history. Print it or save it as PDF.
lab.reportOutputs: The same report including the raw output of every check command (longer).
p.report: Open a printable progress report (domains, weakest topics, all labs) in a new tab. Print it or save it as PDF.
